caseStudy.highlight1: 40,000 events/min ingested with sub-second dashboard queries
caseStudy.highlight2: Time-to-insight cut from 2 days (spreadsheets) to under 1 minute
caseStudy.highlight3: Designed, built and shipped end-to-end in 14 weeks — one person
caseStudy.highlight4: 99.95% uptime over the first 12 months in production
caseStudy.heroCaption: the main dashboard — live event stream, saved views, alerting
caseStudy.problem1: A Belgrade fintech team was flying blind between weekly spreadsheet exports. Product decisions waited days for data that already existed — it just had nowhere to live. They needed a real-time view of user behaviour without buying a six-figure analytics suite.
caseStudy.problem2: The brief: one dashboard, every core metric, fast enough to check between two sips of coffee.
caseStudy.decisions1: Events land in ClickHouse, not Postgres — a columnar store made sub-second aggregation possible on commodity hardware. Postgres keeps what it's good at: users, saved views, alert rules.
caseStudy.decisions2: On the design side: no chart zoo. Four view types, consistent everywhere, so the team reads every screen the same way. Density where it matters, whitespace where it doesn't.
caseStudy.outcome1: The dashboard replaced the weekly export ritual entirely. A year in, it runs at 99.95% uptime and has become the first tab the team opens each morning. Feature decisions that used to wait for Friday's spreadsheet now happen in standup.
